about: The `typeexpr` of a <send> is a string computed from the machine's fields when the send runs, held to the processors the document declares as `sce:types`: the send is delivered by the processor the matching entry names, and a value in none of them is error.execution with nothing sent. `kind` holds the SCXML Event I/O Processor to begin with, so `fire` delivers `landed` to this session. `aim.bogus` makes it a type nothing serves, and `aim.http` a processor this build serves (BasicHTTP) that this send does not declare: each is refused. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: the type the machine holds is a declared one: the event is delivered
and again: the send reads the type each time it runs
the type changes to one nothing serves; nothing is sent
a value in none of the declared types cannot be delivered: error.execution, and nothing sent
the type changes to BasicHTTP, a processor this build serves
this send did not declare it: refused all the same, and nothing sent
the type is a declared one again, and the machine goes on
